message.reasoning_content:
We need answer only JSON. Need evaluate Minimal criterion for each story. We need classify each story. We need determine if any contains extra beyond role, means, optional ends/rationale. Scope individual, so assess each sentence. We need identify violations for comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, etc. Most stories simple "As a ..., I want to ..." maybe with optional so that. Need scrutinize extra details in means like specific technical implementation? Minimal criterion syntactic: contains nothing more than role, means, optional ends/rationale. The means itself can include domain specifics? Need decide if "using content identification or fingerprinting" etc is implementation? The examples penalized "selecting a blue template" as UI detail? But they said "nothing more than role, means, optional ends/rationale. Violation when core story includes comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, or other information that should be external to story sentence." Means may include functionality not implementation? Need careful. User Story traditional: role, means, ends. Means is a capability, can be high-level. Does "search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting" count as implementation hint? "using content identification or fingerprinting" is technology/method. Minimal would arguably violate because implementation details. But these are from backlog maybe all have detailed means. Need apply criterion strictly: If story contains "using content identification or fingerprinting" beyond simple capability? We need assess each story.

Need identify stories with extra info:
- Many have elaboration in the means such as "based on my profile", "based on other users similar to myself", "similar to a given music video based on content similarity", "by exploiting enriched metadata and image tags, so that...", "using automatic speech recognition", "based on automated analysis, citizen annotations, and comments on Talk", "using simple low-level image features", etc. Are these "implementation/testing hints"? Need think.

Criterion Minimal from Lucassen et al: A user story contains nothing more than role, means, and optional ends/rationale. It is syntactic. It might flag stories with extra clauses? Actually "As a <role>, I want <means> so that <ends>" is canonical. Additional "using X" are part of means. But if means includes implementation details, then not minimal? The definition says "contains nothing more than role, means, and optional ends/rationale." That could mean no extra information beyond those three components. If the means itself is long and contains multiple subclauses, still within means. Examples: Example 2 "create a room by entering a title and selecting a blue template" had "selecting a blue template" as UI detail and QA note. They considered "selecting a blue template" a violation because UI/testing details. This means overly specific UI choices in means are non-minimal. But is that because "blue template" is mock-up note? It could be implementation hint. The criterion says "Violation when the core story includes comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, or other information that should be external to the story sentence." So if means includes specific implementation/UI/testing details, violation.

We need evaluate 60 Zooniverse stories. Many are high-level feature stories; some include specific analysis techniques: "simple low-level image features", "automatic speech recognition", "content identification or fingerprinting", "content similarity", "metadata and image tags", "geographical map", "timestamping malfunction", "worm motion analysis", etc. Do these count as implementation hints? I think the Minimal criterion would flag implementation-specific technical means as extra? Let's examine.

The worked example 2: "As a moderator, I want to create a room by entering a title and selecting a blue template, so that members can join. QA: test with 20 users." They highlighted "selecting a blue template" and QA. They did not highlight "entering a title". Why "entering a title" maybe means (functional requirement) acceptable? "selecting a blue template" is UI detail. So some specificity is acceptable, but "blue template" is design detail. The criterion's operational decision rule says comments, mock-up notes, implementation/testing hints, procedural notes, or other information external to story. "blue template" is mock-up/design hint. "store flag in local storage" is implementation note. 

Thus stories with explicit technical approaches like "using content identification or fingerprinting", "based on A/V quality aspects", "using search based on low-level asset information" might be implementation details. But can be seen as part of means: user wants search based on X. Is "content identification or fingerprinting" implementation? Yes, fingerprinting is technical implementation method. But in user story, if user wants search by humming? Hmm.

Need decide likely expected in benchmark. The backlog includes stories with explicit specific techniques: They likely were extracted from project requirements and may have various quality issues. The "Minimal" criterion aims to detect unnecessary details. We need identify stories that have extra information beyond role-means-ends. The extra info may be:
- Comments after story? None have "Note:" or "QA:".
- Some have specific implementation details in the means. Need evaluate each.

Let's list all stories and potential violations.

ZO-001: As a user, I want to search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting.
Contains role, means "search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting." Means includes "using content identification or fingerprinting" = technical implementation? I'd lean Violation: implementation hint. But the user story is about search/discovery capability; specification of fingerprinting could be necessary domain capability? It is an implementation method. Minimal criterion says nothing more than role, means, optional ends. But means can be "search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting"; the "using..." is how, but not necessarily implementation? The task likely expects us to flag such specifics as violation. Need consistency.

ZO-002: As a user, I want to search and discover music based on my profile.
This is role + means only. "based on my profile" is data basis, not implementation. No violation.

ZO-003: As a user, I want to search and discover music based on other users similar to myself.
No violation. Means includes method basis. Not technical.

ZO-004: As a user, I want to search and discover music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity.
"based on content similarity" could be conceptual. No explicit tech. Maybe no violation.

ZO-005: As a user, I want to search and discover music by exploiting enriched metadata and image tags, so that I find related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path.
